title: Search Insert Position
statement:
You are given a list of distinct integers that is already arranged in strictly increasing order, along with a single target integer.

Your job is to determine the index at which the target value is located within the list. If the target does not appear in the list, instead report the index at which it would need to be inserted so that the list remains in sorted (increasing) order.

Because the list is sorted, you should be able to solve this without scanning every element one at a time, an approach that repeatedly narrows the search range by comparing the target to a middle element is expected to achieve the required efficiency.

examples.explanation: The value 7 sits at index 2 in the array, so that index is returned directly.
8 is not present in the array. It falls between 6 (index 2) and 9 (index 3), so inserting it at index 3 keeps the array sorted: [1, 3, 6, 8, 9, 12].

constraints: nums is sorted in strictly increasing order (no duplicate values)
The algorithm must run in O(log n) time
